commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Tetsuo Umezawa ({U}{B}{R}) destroys a tapped OR blocking creature for {U}{B}{B}{R}, tap. Create legal targets through forced combat or exact taps, support continuous colored-mana and untaps, and protect the source while paying four colored mana per destruction.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 4 Optimized — colored-pip-intensive political creature-control with conditional opposing targets. Reversal/Scepter plus productive on-color rocks can supply an infinite untap/mana engine, but needs setup and a legal target for Tetsuo to use it; no generic backup win inserted.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Keep goad/tap/untap and commander-ability copying dominant. No Oracle-less Aura engine, Thoracle/Consultation or Breach generic Grixis shell; free protection and draw serve four-pip activated removal.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: 99/99 original noncommander physical copies reviewed individually in the 99slot CSV. Eighty KEEP and 19 CUT. Source role table comes from Oct20 authored M6 review, and each deleted physical copy has a named replacement. Retain eight-plus untap, six-plus target makers, ten on-theme goad/political pieces and powerful colored rocks; replace delayed and generic actions with reusable direct tap, death untap, protection and strict pip-fixing.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: 35 front-face lands, one Soporific Springs MDFC = 36 land-capable cards, Maze of Ith produces no mana. Initial sixteen basics become Island3/Mountain3/Swamp4; two Islands, two Mountains and two Swamps plus Sulfur Falls become Otawara/Morphic Pool, City of Brass/Mana Confluence, Takenuma/Urborg and Forbidden Orchard. This creates multiple new B and any-color sources to pay UBBR repeatedly. Life loss and nonbasic hate are actual tradeoffs; colored signets/talismans stay.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Keep Bedevil, Chaos Warp, Terminate, Withering Torment, Mana Drain, Force of Will, Cyclonic Rift, Vandalblast, Damnation, Rakdos Charm and Swiftfoot Boots/Lightning Greaves. Fierce/Swat protect without tapping needed UBBR. Deluge can spare 3-toughness Tetsuo at X2, but losing Propaganda and Counterspell increases defense and creature-spell-response risks.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: An equipped Tetsuo copies the UBBR destroy activation for one extra generic rather than Rings' two; haste on the equipped creature also handles a recast.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Requires casting a three-mana red artifact and paying equip two, whereas Rings can copy activated abilities of other permanents without equipping.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Any-color land supplies whichever activation pip is missing instead of a fifth single-red basic, especially the second black.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Costs one life whenever tapped for mana and is vulnerable to nonbasic-land hate.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: With Tetsuo controlled, redirecting an opponent's targeted removal or stack interaction while retaining UBBR for activation is stronger than a three-mana passive attack tax.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Does not stop board wipes, untargeted removal or an attack in a two-player endgame; Propaganda was a defensive floor.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: At instant speed readies Tetsuo plus all nonland permanents, and with Isochron Scepter and productive colored rocks creates repeatable mana/untap access rather than one black burst.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Alone it requires an established board and does not untap lands; one-shot Dark Ritual could accelerate a black-heavy early turn.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: A free noncreature counter when Tetsuo is present preserves all four colored mana to destroy threats while answering interaction.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Cannot counter creatures and costs 2U when the commander is absent, unlike Counterspell's unconditional UU.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Turns conditional U/R dual into untapped U/B/R source for Tetsuo, and Spirits given to opponents can later be goaded or destroyed once tapped.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Every activation gifts an opposing 1/1 flying token; those tokens may pressure us and enter untapped.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Four-mana artifact can pay one and tap an active utility creature during an opponent's upkeep, then make Tetsuo's destroy ability immediately relevant; Geode costs six plus a future landfall.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Single target at once and one-mana extra activation; loses Rager's repeatable entire-player goad and first strike body.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Imprinting Reversal converts the existing colored-rock suite into repeated Tetsuo and rock untaps, potentially positive colored mana with three or more mana per iteration.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Two-card setup needs an instant in hand and multiple productive rocks; Brainstorm gave immediate one-blue selection with fetch shuffles.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Four-mana creature supplies each opponent a permanently goaded hasty first-striking trample token, and the tokens become tapped Tetsuo targets when they attack.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Gives real threats to opponents, and tokens can attack Cory in endgame or when other opponents cannot be attacked; Fumiko forced every opposing creature to attack.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: In multiplayer the UB dual supplies either blue or an additional source for Tetsuo's double-black activation where an Island could only supply blue.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Enters tapped in heads-up play or after opponents have been eliminated; fewer fetchable basics remain.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Artifact is usable the turn it enters to tap any creature for a Tetsuo target or untap Tetsuo for another payable activation, without a sick creature body.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Two mana per activation and only one target; Sly's persistent goad and evasion manipulation could be superior in a slow political table.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Opponents' spells now generate either cards or mana taxes; keeps removal/protection available without giving opponent cards as Xantcha's activated draw can.
weakest_slots.reasoning: The trigger can be paid for and Study is a generic Grixis power card; Xantcha created a distinct shared political damage outlet.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Preserves B production and channels back a lost untap creature such as Aphetto Alchemist or Puppeteer, with a discount while Tetsuo is on board.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Milling three may be undesirable in some draws, and it is a nonbasic rather than an easily searched basic Swamp.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Each creature killed by Tetsuo normally dies, untapping the equipped commander for another payable UBBR activation; extra death events also reset him.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Equip four and no extra colored mana make setup costly; Grenzo's two-mana body could goad or generate card access through combat connections.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: For three mana and X life, X=2 clears small utility creatures while Tetsuo stays a 1/1 until end of turn; Act's 13 damage kills our whole tap/untap setup.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Paying life can be severe against large creatures and Deluge may leave high-toughness threats without a high X.

weakest_slots.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Three-mana enchantment makes creatures played by opponents enter tapped two turns sooner than Urabrask's five-mana symmetrical haste/entry lock, so new utility creatures start as legal Tetsuo targets.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Does not grant our team haste and does not cover every token entering; Urabrask's broader two-sided effect wins some high-mana games.

weakest_slots.weakness: Untaps Tetsuo or another permanent, and cycling offers an immediate untap card draw.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep for the target/answer role: Rathi's cheap repeatable B tap directly manufactures legal targets; Vizier cannot tap opposing creatures and its cycling needs two mana plus discarded card.

weakest_slots.weakness: Cheap 1B creature reduces red/blue spell generic requirements and can block.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep for the target/answer role: Tetsuo's cast cost UBR and destroy cost UBBR contain no generic symbols, so a spell discount cannot cure the central activation bottleneck; Bedevil answers artifacts/planeswalkers.

weakest_slots.weakness: Provides a repeatable tap mode and kill-tapped mode in one 1UB body.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep for the target/answer role: Its tap costs 3U or kill 3B plus tap and summoning sickness, much slower than Royal Assassin's free kill and current Crown/Strings tap.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: The Oct15 approved 14-swap tap/untap list is commander-first, legal and internally coherent. M6 deep review/Grok advisory identified Icy versus Geode but held it for payable enemy-upkeep comparison. M7 reconsiders all of that rather than treating historical HOLD as final.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: EDHREC Tetsuo base Top Cards/High Lift, forced-combat and tap/untap tags, 162 unfiltered decks but 10/3 tagged samples. Current 93-card live Scryfall Oracle and 25 material decisions. Existing M6/Grok/Pass C research, alternate exact physical 18/21 swap lists, and fresh off-ranking Reversal/Scepter/Staff and utility-land research.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: Off-ranking Scepter/Reversal and Thornbite Staff unlock repeated colored-rock/Tetsuo access; Battlemage reduces copy cost and adds haste; precision artifacts address opponents' nonattacking utility creatures. Additional Vizier, Nightscape, Stalking Assassin, Ensnare and Angler candidates weaken target coverage or answers in larger portfolios.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Nineteen justified physical swaps, twelve nonland and seven color-base changes: better exact tap, repeated untaps/death cascades, free commander protection, selective sweep and more UBBR sources. Costs are weaker generic combat defense, one fewer blanket counter and more nonbasic/life exposure. On-theme line count stays high and no generic terminal combo inserted.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: An equipped Tetsuo copies the UBBR destroy activation for one extra generic rather than Rings' two; haste on the equipped creature also handles a recast.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Requires casting a three-mana red artifact and paying equip two, whereas Rings can copy activated abilities of other permanents without equipping.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Any-color land supplies whichever activation pip is missing instead of a fifth single-red basic, especially the second black.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Costs one life whenever tapped for mana and is vulnerable to nonbasic-land hate.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: With Tetsuo controlled, redirecting an opponent's targeted removal or stack interaction while retaining UBBR for activation is stronger than a three-mana passive attack tax.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Does not stop board wipes, untargeted removal or an attack in a two-player endgame; Propaganda was a defensive floor.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: At instant speed readies Tetsuo plus all nonland permanents, and with Isochron Scepter and productive colored rocks creates repeatable mana/untap access rather than one black burst.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Alone it requires an established board and does not untap lands; one-shot Dark Ritual could accelerate a black-heavy early turn.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: A free noncreature counter when Tetsuo is present preserves all four colored mana to destroy threats while answering interaction.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Cannot counter creatures and costs 2U when the commander is absent, unlike Counterspell's unconditional UU.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Turns conditional U/R dual into untapped U/B/R source for Tetsuo, and Spirits given to opponents can later be goaded or destroyed once tapped.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Every activation gifts an opposing 1/1 flying token; those tokens may pressure us and enter untapped.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Four-mana artifact can pay one and tap an active utility creature during an opponent's upkeep, then make Tetsuo's destroy ability immediately relevant; Geode costs six plus a future landfall.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Single target at once and one-mana extra activation; loses Rager's repeatable entire-player goad and first strike body.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Imprinting Reversal converts the existing colored-rock suite into repeated Tetsuo and rock untaps, potentially positive colored mana with three or more mana per iteration.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Two-card setup needs an instant in hand and multiple productive rocks; Brainstorm gave immediate one-blue selection with fetch shuffles.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Four-mana creature supplies each opponent a permanently goaded hasty first-striking trample token, and the tokens become tapped Tetsuo targets when they attack.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Gives real threats to opponents, and tokens can attack Cory in endgame or when other opponents cannot be attacked; Fumiko forced every opposing creature to attack.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: In multiplayer the UB dual supplies either blue or an additional source for Tetsuo's double-black activation where an Island could only supply blue.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Enters tapped in heads-up play or after opponents have been eliminated; fewer fetchable basics remain.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Artifact is usable the turn it enters to tap any creature for a Tetsuo target or untap Tetsuo for another payable activation, without a sick creature body.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Two mana per activation and only one target; Sly's persistent goad and evasion manipulation could be superior in a slow political table.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Opponents' spells now generate either cards or mana taxes; keeps removal/protection available without giving opponent cards as Xantcha's activated draw can.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: The trigger can be paid for and Study is a generic Grixis power card; Xantcha created a distinct shared political damage outlet.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Preserves B production and channels back a lost untap creature such as Aphetto Alchemist or Puppeteer, with a discount while Tetsuo is on board.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Milling three may be undesirable in some draws, and it is a nonbasic rather than an easily searched basic Swamp.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Each creature killed by Tetsuo normally dies, untapping the equipped commander for another payable UBBR activation; extra death events also reset him.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Equip four and no extra colored mana make setup costly; Grenzo's two-mana body could goad or generate card access through combat connections.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: For three mana and X life, X=2 clears small utility creatures while Tetsuo stays a 1/1 until end of turn; Act's 13 damage kills our whole tap/untap setup.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Paying life can be severe against large creatures and Deluge may leave high-toughness threats without a high X.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Incumbent challenge: Three-mana enchantment makes creatures played by opponents enter tapped two turns sooner than Urabrask's five-mana symmetrical haste/entry lock, so new utility creatures start as legal Tetsuo targets.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Does not grant our team haste and does not cover every token entering; Urabrask's broader two-sided effect wins some high-mana games.

low_swap_heightened_audit.off_ranked_opportunities: The off-ranking key is repeatable Scepter/Dramatic colored-rock untap and Thornbite Staff kill-trigger reset, plus Battlemage's Bracers and land-channel/all-color source improvement.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: An exact complete 100 retaining original Geode Rager and Sly Instigator and adding Vizier instead of Rathi. Goad breadth wins in creature-swarm tables but weakens immediate upkeep tap and kill timing.
A complete 21-swap 100 adds Vizier/Familiar by cutting Rathi/Bedevil. Additional generic discounts and cycling lose the cheap repeat target maker and artifact/planeswalker removal.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Icy versus Geode is revisited with turn-four artifact and five total mana paid versus six-plus-landfall body, on enemy upkeep or before attackers. Frozen Aether's multi-player permanent-entry denial is preserved; Sly instead of Geode and Fumiko are alternate cuts judged weaker. Previous M6 'HOLD' not copied.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Six-mana Geode requires landfall and future attack to make a target; Sly waits through creature summoning sickness; original double-black availability is stressed by six red/blue-only basics and a conditional UR dual.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: The complete 19-change chosen package generates ready target conditions, colored payments and untaps while preserving direct goad identity. The 21-change package is rejected on target-access and answer-coverage grounds, not because nineteen is a target.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: Post-five floor audit revisited every original 99 physical slot including all 16 original basic lands, spell-to-colored mana tradeoffs, copy/haste redundancy, timed tap preconditions, and losses of blanket removal/pillowfort. The present 19 is not a cap: the complete 21-swap alternative was evaluated, and three further retained incumbent roles Bedevil, Rathi Trapper and Royal Assassin faced named new challengers.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Keep the BBR instant that removes artifacts/planeswalkers; Nightscape reduces generic only, while both Tetsuo cast UBR and activate UBBR have zero generic.
Keep two-mana repeatable enemy tap; Vizier's cycling untap can reset Tetsuo once but cannot make a nonattacker become a legal tapped target.
Keep backup free tap-to-kill; Stalking's 3U or 3B tap/kill activations are prohibitively generic expensive versus existing cheaper sources.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Add Vizier and Nightscape on top of all 19 selected changes to increase untap cycling and spell discount in a complete 100.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: It sacrifices Bedevil artifact/planeswalker removal and Rathi cheap direct tap; Nightscape's generic discount has no bearing on UBR casting Tetsuo or his UBBR destruction activation.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: The decisive metric is payable, protected UBBR removal opportunities with actual legal tapped/blocking targets. The remaining challengers either delay exact tap creation, cannot reduce colored activation costs, lose uncommon artifact/planeswalker answers, or require untenable mana setup. Source and finite rules checks support this stopping judgment independently of any swap count.
